headline: Town boards split recommendations on Special Town Meeting warrant articles ahead of October 17, while departments prepared for potential tax override budget cuts.
synopsis: Ahead of the October 17 Special Town Meeting, the Select Board and Advisory Committee took opposing positions on several warrant articles, with both boards opposing additional Community Preservation Act funds for the Peninsula Trail footbridge while disagreeing on golf course irrigation and two-family zoning. The Conservation Commission voted to request that the Select Board retain 100,000 dollars in unissued borrowing authority for Breakneck Hill Farm restoration rather than rescinding the full authorization. Across town departments, including the Library, Board of Health, and Conservation Commission, officials prepared two FY28 budget scenarios, evaluating steep reductions to staff hours and library services in the event an anticipated spring tax override fails. Land use boards also advanced zoning bylaw revisions and continued review of several commercial and residential developments.

highlights.title: Select Board endorses seven Special Town Meeting articles
highlights.why: The Select Board voted to recommend seven of eight warrant articles, supporting golf course irrigation and two-family zoning amendments while voting 1-4 against 217,318 dollars in CPA funding for a Peninsula Trail pedestrian bridge.

highlights.title: Advisory Committee rejects CPA requests and two-family zoning
highlights.why: The committee voted against recommending CPA funding for golf course irrigation and the Peninsula Trail footbridge, as well as two-family zoning amendments, while endorsing an appointed town clerk and establishing a stormwater enterprise fund.

highlights.title: Library reviews severe cuts under override failure scenario
highlights.why: Under town instructions to prepare two FY28 budgets ahead of a planned spring tax override ballot question, library trustees reviewed a fallback scenario that would eliminate programming, staff training, and travel, and reduce database subscriptions by over half.

highlights.title: Conservation Commission seeks to keep Breakneck Hill borrowing authority
highlights.why: The commission voted 4-1 to request that the Select Board retain 100,000 dollars in unissued borrowing capacity to ensure adequate funding for soil de-compaction, trail work, and vernal pool restoration rather than fully rescinding 727,000 dollars at Town Meeting.

highlights.title: ZBA finalizes two-family dwelling zoning bylaw language
highlights.why: The board approved modified text for Article 2 on the Special Town Meeting warrant, eliminating the two-year waiting period to convert single-family homes into two-family dwellings and clarifying definitions.

looking_ahead.what: Select Board special virtual meeting to reopen and sign the revised Special Town Meeting warrant
Planning Board public hearings on Costco major site plan and two-family dwelling zoning bylaw
